text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Singapore Education Minister Teo Chee Hean says there are three priorities for Singapore's education system as it heads into 21st century: developing creativity, exploiting information technology, and emphasising national education.
- Fourteen leading technology companies will invest more than Singapore $100 million over next two years to develop multimedia applications and services called Singapore ONE.
- Up to 5,000 households and offices will be linked electronically for island-wide trial of Singapore ONE network by end of year.
- Korean unit of personal computer maker IPC Corporation fails to to repay 570 million won in promissory notes.
- Singapore Economic Development Board expects to attract Singapore $8.5 billion worth of investments this year and $10 billion by 2000.
- Hutchinson IntraPage outbid incumbent service provider Singapore Telecom to become infrastructure provider for paging signals in the North-East MRT line.
- Singaporeans charge S$7 billion worth of purchases to credit and charge cards last year.
- Imperial Hotel, owned by mainboard-listed Hind Hotels International, seeks to redevelop site into condominiums.
- Japanese Yen advances against U.S. dollar after comments by Japanese Finance Ministry official.
- Amcol Holdings' judicial managers in Mauritius trying to recover company's S$56 million investment in proposed resort and property development.
- Iqbal Jumabhoy says option given to brother Rafiq is invalid.
- Omni Industries receives in-principle approval from Stock Exchange of Singapore for primary listing.
- Listed NatSteel forms joint venture with two parties to develop Australian $100 million residential and service apartment project in Sydney, Australia.
- ASJ Holdings will allocate 27 percent of initial public offer shares to small investors.
